title: Why One Apple Half Goes Brown (and Lemon Stops It) #science #kitchen
description:
Cut an apple in half and leave it out: one half can go brown while the other stays white. It isn't rot. Cutting bursts the apple's cells, and an enzyme called polyphenol oxidase (PPO), normally kept apart from the fruit's polyphenols, spills out and meets them. With oxygen from the air, the enzyme turns the polyphenols into quinones, which react and clump into brown pigments. The white half got lemon juice: the acid slows the enzyme, and the vitamin C (ascorbic acid) turns quinones back before they can go brown.

Try it: cut an apple, brush one half with lemon juice, and check both after 10 to 20 minutes. Different apple varieties brown at different speeds. The brown part is safe to eat; it only changes colour and a little flavour.
